primary.question: Under which circumstances can a concern or complaint be made under this University of Essex whistleblowing policy?
primary.expected_answer: A concern or complaint can be raised if it is in the public interest, i.e., it involves serious wrongdoing that has an impact beyond the individual making the disclosure.
primary.actual_answer:
Concerns or disclosures that are in the public interest, meaning they involve serious wrongdoing with an impact beyond the individual making the disclosure, can be raised under the University of Essex's Whistleblowing Policy. These concerns must relate to malpractice and the disclosure must be made in accordance with the policy’s procedures and in the reasonable belief that it tends to show malpractice and is in the public interest [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/policy-whistleblowing.pdf].

If concerns are solely of a personal nature, they must be raised under the Code of Student Conduct or the Student Concerns and Complaints Procedure [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/policy-whistleblowing.pdf].

follow_up.actual_answer:
Following receipt of a disclosure, the designated person will acknowledge it in writing within 10 working days and may discuss next steps with People and Culture or another senior independent staff member [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/policy-whistleblowing.pdf]. The outcome of any investigation will be reported to the designated officer, who will consider further actions, potentially including referral under the Disciplinary Procedure [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/policy-whistleblowing.pdf]. The individual raising the concern will be kept informed of progress and may have an opportunity to contribute or comment on decisions [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/policy-whistleblowing.pdf]. Feedback will be given within 3 months, and a central record of disclosures (excluding the individual's name) will be kept by People and Culture [https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/policy-whistleblowing.pdf].
